request.spec:
The consolidated figures gain, per grade on any sheet of the tree, the due-totals of the people on
that grade (retired people left out) added up over the tree, and per status the count of claims in
that status over the tree.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The consolidated figures gain, per grade on any sheet of the tree, the due-totals of the people on
that grade (retired people left out) added up over the tree, and per status the count of claims in
that status over the tree.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The consolidated figures now show, for each grade (A, B, C), the due-total of that grade's people (retired people left out) added up over the whole sheet tree. They also show, for each claim status, how many claims have it across the tree. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The whole change is in `src/main/frontend/features/consolidated/consolidated.slot.tsx`; the server and stored data didn't need to change. The panel already added up each sheet's totals over the tree in the front end, and the new figures work the same way:

- **Per grade:** for each sheet, it adds up the due-totals of the non-retired people on each grade. It uses the same helpers as the Summary panel, so a grade's consolidated figure is the sum of what each sheet's own summary shows for it.
- **Per status:** for each sheet, it counts the claims in each status, then adds the counts up over the tree.
- **On screen:** the new values carry the test ids `consolidated-grade-<A|B|C>-due-total` and `consolidated-status-<STATUS>-count`.

The panel updates when any of these figures changes. I keyed that on a string built from the per-grade and per-status values, which meant adding an `eslint-disable` comment for one hooks rule. The codebase already uses that kind of comment in `claims.slot.tsx`.
